transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I’m just... I'm exhausted. And it's in a way that sleep doesn’t really fix. I mean, I'm used to being busy, but lately, just getting through a normal workday and then managing dinner at home... it all just feels a lot heavier than it should.
Beyond feeling exhausted, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless lately?
Yeah, I have. Um... most days lately, I just wake up with this heavy, gray feeling. It's sort of like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about a month now. Um... before that, I was actually feeling the exact opposite. I had a stretch where I was unusually energized, just really driven and getting a ton done. But this recent swing down into feeling persistently low... yeah, that's been going on for about a month.
During that period when you were feeling unusually energized and driven, did that state interfere significantly with your ability to work or maintain your personal relationships?

No, not during that energized time. That actually felt pretty productive, so it didn't really cause problems at work or with my family. 

It's more so this current low period that's affecting things. I mean, I’m still showing up for my job and handling my home responsibilities, but... I’ve been a lot slower with making decisions. And I'm definitely less reliable with family plans right now. I've also found myself a lot more withdrawn from the art activities that usually keep me connected to people.
Looking back further than these past two months, have you ever experienced similar periods of feeling unusually energized or, conversely, feeling this low?

Yeah, I have. Um... the longest depressed stretch I can clearly remember actually lasted about five months. During that time, I just felt really low, tired, and... well, just unlike myself most days. So, yes, I've definitely experienced this kind of low before.
Looking back at your life overall, how many separate, distinct periods of that high-energy, driven state have you experienced, including the one you mentioned?
I'm honestly not sure exactly how many. I haven't really kept a count... um, I know I've had a few of them over the years, including this most recent one, but I couldn't give you an exact number.
During those high-energy periods you've had in the past, did people around you notice a distinct change in your behavior or personality, even if it didn't cause problems in your life?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um... no one ever actually said anything to me about it. If they did notice a change, they probably just thought I was having a highly productive week at work or just in a really good mood. But no, nobody ever pointed it out as being, you know, distinctly different or unusual.
During those high-energy periods you mentioned, did that feeling of being unusually driven and energized typically last for at least four days in a row?
Yeah, definitely. When I get like that, it's not just a day or two. It usually lasts for at least four days, sometimes a bit longer, where I just have that constant drive and energy going.
During those high-energy periods, did you find that you needed significantly less sleep than usual to feel fully rested?

Yes, absolutely. During that stretch, I was sleeping maybe... four hours a night? And I wasn't tired at all. I'd wake up feeling completely rested and just ready to go—like, ready to send out work emails, sketch out ideas for upcoming events, or even just reorganize the kitchen before the sun came up. It was definitely a lot less sleep than I normally need.
During those high-energy periods when you needed less sleep, did you find that your thoughts were racing or moving so quickly that you had trouble keeping up with them?

Yeah, I did. Um, the best way I can describe it is that my mind felt like it had too many tabs open at once. I would just have all these ideas for work, things for the cultural group I'm involved in, and our whole household schedule all racing through my head together. It was just a lot of thoughts moving really quickly all at the same time.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel unusually important, powerful, or like you had special talents or abilities beyond your normal self?

Yeah, I think so. Um, I was honestly convinced that I could fix the whole department morale problem at work, and even our family routines at home. I just felt like I had the perfect solution for everything, and if everyone would just get on board with my plan, it would all be fixed. So, yeah, I definitely felt unusually capable during those times.

During any of those high-energy periods, was the change in your behavior ever so intense or disruptive that it led to you being hospitalized, or caused such significant problems that you were unable to function at work or in your daily life?

No, nothing like that. I've never been hospitalized for it. I mean, I was definitely more intense and probably a bit much for the people around me, but I was still going to work every day and getting things done. It never got to a point where I couldn't function or anything. I just felt really driven.
